title: THE FESTIVAL OF TWO GRAVITIES

rounds.summary: R14 preflight. Concrete aim: keep the Turnhouse axle from failing while allowing Vale and Orra to remember their dead in the bodily direction each community called home. Coherent counterparts: previously displaced Vale wants its skyward rite to begin without another assigned last place; Orra wants its expanded stoneward naming to preserve the direction in which its vane dead actually died. The strongest objection is explicit: a clever sequence can become another demand to dilute identity. Illuminara therefore witnesses both full rites, bears an Orra disc in Vale pull and a Vale bell in Orra pull, and does not propose order until she understands that direction is part of each sentence. The first mechanically equal test fails because it compresses Vale’s seven breaths into Orra’s three; a memorial panel cracks and the remaining clock shortens. The redesigned half-turn preserves distinct words, pauses and directions. Orra freely accepts Vale first for today after hearing the displacement account; both communities retain stop authority; an elder from each side keeps a separate outside rite without penalty. Illuminara braces and arrests physical load only. She does not touch minds, assign the first turn or manufacture agreement. Concrete positive result: the axle survives, every shared-chamber name is carried through both orientations, Vale begins without subordination, Orra names its dead in true ring-down, and a jointly maintained two-key memorial mechanism is established. Remaining costs are visible: the cracked panel seam, the failed test, separate rites and no permanent settlement of future order.

A strong first draft with a living idea: two communities who need opposite directions to name their dead, rites that are specific and different, a Vale-first turn that Orra accepts freely and that Sela refuses to let become a reward for usefulness, elders on both sides who walk out and keep their own rites, and a cost that is real (the cracked panel, the failed test, no settlement of next year's order). The R14 core is met on the page: Illuminara learns that direction is part of each sentence, which is why no substitute hall will do; care becomes act (Sela's hand on Lio's tray, Teren listening to the eighteen names); the turn is acceptance and not power, since she only holds torsion. Three bounded problems remain. First, the physics of the half-turn is not consistent: which way the floor faces during each rite, and what the degrees stand for, cannot be reconciled between scenes three, four and six, and the closing claim that every name was spoken in both orientations is not what the story stages. Second, the two decisive moves, the discovery that the opposed loads can drive a turn and the equal-pause test that cracks the panel, pass through Jori and others, so her intelligence is visible in the early scenes but not at the hinge, and the failure has no owner although she let the test run after hearing both objections. Third, the ending is image and action but is wrapped in a ledger paragraph and signed terms, the climax replays litanies that scenes two and three already gave in full, and the draft is well above the usual length.

Bounded S2 revision answering Claude T02 P1–P3. It fixes the orientation mechanics as a preset Vale-down chamber, complete Vale naming, one opposed-load half-turn, then complete Orra naming. Illuminara infers the coupled turn from the sideways disc and rising bell drop before Jori confirms it. The shortened test is an explicit shared risk recommendation for which Illuminara accepts responsibility. The first cooling wedge, forty-minute load window and midpoint wedge reconcile the 08:56–09:47 clock. The ending is compressed while preserving both full rites, the crack and seam, elders outside, apprentices, children, two keys and Illuminara’s delight.

A real improvement on T01. The orientation bookkeeping now holds: the empty room is preset Vale-down, Vale names in its own direction while its belts store lift, Orra loads silently, the opposed stored loads make one half-turn, Orra names in Orra-down. The clock reconciles (wedge by 09:15, rite 09:20-09:47), Illuminara owns the shortened-test recommendation in one clear line, Sela refuses to let usefulness become the reason for Vale-first, and the ending now rests on images (four seconds of floating drops, Nemi's laugh, Sela's hand on Lio's tray, two keys in two boxes) instead of a ledger. Three bounded problems remain. First, the solution is stated by Jori in scene one, before Illuminara has felt either pull, and again in scene three and scene five, so her composing insight confirms a plan already on the table and the idea is told three times. Second, the shortened test is the story's one real risk but its necessity is thin: she has already shown the loads compose with a disc and a bell cord, and Jori says the test would teach almost nothing if stopped early, so her call can read as careless rather than a trade taken with open eyes; what the failure actually teaches is not tied to what follows. Third, the number ledger and the tray/belt bookkeeping still get in the way: several figures that do not bite, three different 'forties', and Orra both 'loading a tray in each pause' and standing with 'hands away from loaded trays'.

Final bounded revision answering Claude T04 P1–P3 without reopening the selected concept. Scene one now states only the opposed-load constraint and three meaningful clocks; Illuminara’s sideways-disc and rising-drop experiment becomes the first complete solution. The live test names two unique questions, and its break directly determines full seven-breath settling and Vale-first loading on the unbroken face. The plan is spelled out once, tray and belt jobs are consistent, and the wedge equation is explicit: forty minutes for a twenty-seven-minute rite.

T05 answers the three bounded T04 points. (P1) The composing insight now originates with Illuminara: scene one keeps only the motor lockout, the opposed-load constraint and Jori's unanswered problem; her sideways disc and rising drop are the first appearance of the idea ('Not cancelling. Composing.'), Jori confirms it and states the preset, name, load, turn, name sequence once, and scene five keeps only the new order learned from the break. (P2) The shortened test now has a stated reason (whether a real belt settles before the counterweight takes it, and which face of the damaged tooth takes the hand-off), and the break answers both: the counterweight struck while the second belt still oscillated and the shock crossed the already damaged face, which is why all seven Vale breaths and Vale-first loading on the unbroken face are required; Sela still refuses usefulness as the reason for priority. (P3) The ledger is cleaned: 17 minutes (old collar), 19 (brace clock), 27 (rite) and 40 (wedge) each have one role; Orra adds measured discs to one common tray on the last breath; Vale's belts explicitly change job from lifting mourners to storing the drum's pull. The timeline reconciles (rehearsals from 08:13, joint naming 09:20, last Orra name 09:47, wedge seated 09:14). Seven scenes in R10 speaker-labelled format, about 2,860 words.

final_critic_line: Two communities who each needed the other's hour to be the wrong one learned that the room could turn if their pulls were composed rather than ranked, and Illuminara, who had held an Orra disc in Vale's gravity to learn how wrong feels, owned the shortened test that cracked the tooth and the panel, so Teren chose to let Vale begin, Sela put a hand on Lio's tray through the turn, and two keys went into two boxes.
